entries.name: Road Run
entries.reason: Source-bound side-view draft of a stride run on the spot, since a preview cannot travel. Tall with a small forward lean; each leg goes through landing beneath the body, mid-stance, toe-off, heel coming up behind, knee driving through and reaching down to land, with the two legs half a stride apart and the arms swinging opposite the legs. Between each toe-off and the next landing both feet are off the ground. The pace is even through the stride. Not drawn: breathing and effort, which the source describes and a figure cannot show.
entries.summary: Run tall with relaxed shoulders and a small lean from the ankles, each foot landing quietly beneath the body, at a pace you can hold.

frames.caption: Begin tall with the shoulders relaxed and a small whole-body lean from the ankles.
Let each foot land quietly beneath the body.
Push off, keeping the stride relaxed.
Both feet leave the ground, then the other foot lands beneath the body.
Keep the shoulders and hands relaxed.
Settle into a pace you can hold.
If breathing or form changes sharply, slow to a sustainable effort.
